newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Hong Kong businesses seek entry to ASEAN market.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong businesses seek entry to ASEAN market.

text.p: Hong Kong businessmen are looking at the Philippines as their entry point to the growing ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA), a leader of a Hong Kong investment mission to the Philippines said on Wednesday.

Sidney Fung, assistant director for international affairs of the Hong Kong General Chamber of Commerce, said Hong Kong businessmen are exploring investment opportunities in southeast Asia after China tightened its investment regulations for foreign companies.
"They are looking around the region for investment opportunities ... It is getting difficult to invest in China because of many regulations and increased red tape," Fung said.
The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) comprises of the Philippines, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam and Brunei.
ASEAN countries have agreed to form a free trade area by the turn of the century.
Fung said the businessmen were not here to look for possible relocation after the handover of the colony to China next year.
Many delegates said they were here to forge possible tie usp with Philippine businesses.

The 30-member delegation began its four-day mission to the country on Wednesday by meeting with local businessmen at a "business matching session". They are sheduled to visit the Subic freeport area and other special economic zones in northern Philippines.
The delegation included businessmen with interests in fruits and seafood, banking and finance, brokerage, shipping, plastics, and jewellery.
